responses.any_presentation: Every well-formed presentation writes a receipt pair (presentation / disposition) and returns {pair_id, disposition, tier, payment_txid, chain}. Settlement is recorded at presentation; the transfer already landed.
responses.excess: The landed amount must cover the tier price; any excess is recorded in the pair and is not refunded.
refusal_codes: PAYMENT_ALREADY_CONSUMED (a txid crosses exactly once; the receipt chain is the registry)
PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND (not yet confirmed; re-present after confirmation — not consumed)
EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE (chain read failed; re-present the same txid once reads recover — not consumed)
refusal_fields: the six-field grammar (failure_code, failed_predicate, required_evidence_or_repair, retry_entrypoint, owning_goal, next_attempt)

crossing_4lph4.step_1_transfer: Send a TRC-20 USDT transfer to the receptor for at least the tier price. On Tron the address and the contract are the asset: cross-check both against GET /offer before transferring.

payload.note: Optional; its SHA-256 is recorded on the pair.

request.note: {counterparty, action, scope_ref, evidence: {authority, delegation, evidence_refs, exclusions, policy, validity_at_commit}} — decided by the production evaluator, the same evaluate() the 8374 endpoint serves.

challenge.body: x402 v1 PaymentRequired JSON (see example_challenge). accepts[0].maxAmountRequired is the TOTAL for this crossing in micro-USDC: the tier governance fee plus the settlement charge quoted live at challenge time (settlement_charge_quote carries the quote and its formula).
challenge.fail_closed: If no live settlement-charge quote can be produced, the endpoint answers 503 FAIL_CLOSED (SETTLEMENT_CHARGE_QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE, or SETTLEMENT_QUOTE_STALE_BEYOND_BOUND when the last good quote is older than 300s) and issues no challenge. Retry later; nothing was consumed.

headers.PAYMENT-REQUIRED: base64 of the x402 v2 PaymentRequired object for the same terms; its accepts[0].amount equals the v1 total.

payment_presentation.amount_rule: Authorize the challenge's total exactly. The amount is the tier governance fee plus the settlement charge quoted in that challenge; settlement gas is charged on the crossing, never absorbed.
payment_presentation.signing: Any conformant x402 client library can produce the header. The reference client shipped with this schema performs every step except the signature itself, and returns the exact object to sign.

v1.value: base64 of {x402Version: 1, scheme: 'exact', network: 'eip155:8453', payload: {signature, authorization: {from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce}}} where the authorization is an EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization signed under the USDC EIP-712 domain on Base (name 'USD Coin', version '2'), to = payTo, value = the challenge total.

v2.value: base64 of {x402Version: 2, accepted: {scheme, network, amount, asset, payTo, maxTimeoutSeconds, extra}, payload: {signature, authorization: {from, to, value, validAfter, validBefore, nonce}}} with the same EIP-3009 core.

counterparty.note: The caller's identifier; recorded on the pair.

scope_ref.note: The admitted scope the request is evaluated against, e.g. ME-EVAL-01.

sublane.note: Optional routing name; receipts land on the sub-lane chain. An invalid sublane is a FAIL_CLOSED refusal on the parent chain.

tier.note: An unknown tier coerces to receipt-only.

fields: pair_anchor_terminal (= the pair's second record hash; anchor your copy to it)
allow.v2_note: v2 payers also receive a PAYMENT-RESPONSE header.

fields: the six-field detail spread at top level (failure_code, failed_predicate, required_evidence_or_repair, retry_entrypoint, owning_goal, next_attempt)
non_allow_paid.note: A paid NON-ALLOW still issues its pair and the fee is still paid. Provider-side FAIL_CLOSED refusals never settle.

payment_failure.body: FAIL_CLOSED with a refusal pair (refusal_pair_id, refusal_record_pair) and metering. The authorization was not settled.

settlement_charge_quote.formula: ceil(gas_units_basis * (2*base_fee_per_gas + priority_fee_per_gas) * eth_usd / 1e18, to the next micro-USDC)

example_challenge.error: payment required: the governed crossing bears the posted fee under the active pricing mode
example_challenge.note: Captured live from POST https://8374.stegverse.org/crossing, 2026-11-24, tier receipt-only, unpaid. The settlement charge moves with live Base gas; the governance fee does not.

4LPH4.chain_export: GET /chain4.json — a JSON document {verdict, problems, entries, pairs, terminal_anchor, segment: [entries]}
4LPH4.payment: TRC-20 transfer to the receptor, then present the txid (no EIP-3009 on Tron)

8374.payment: x402 exact scheme, EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization, dual-stack v1 + v2

receipt_pair.form_4LPH4: Two chain entries sharing one pair_id, kinds PAIR_A (presentation) and PAIR_B (disposition). Entry shape: {body, hash, kind, pair_id, prev, seq}. Settlement, when it lands, is recorded at presentation; later settlement records append as their own entries.
receipt_pair.form_8374: Two chain entries sharing one pair_id. Entry shape: {content, hash, i, prev}. content carries pair_id, index_in_pair (0 then 1), side, kind, the crossing, the disposition, and ts. The second entry's content carries pair_anchor = the first entry's hash.
receipt_pair.retention_bundle: Every 8374 crossing response carries a RETENTION_BUNDLE/1: {bundle, rules_version: 'receipt-chain-rules/1', chain, pair_id, exported_from_anchor, span: {anchor_before_span: 'GENESIS', entries (genesis through the pair's second member), anchor_after_span}, pair, settles, settlement_reference, segment_seal}. Keep it: it lets you verify the pair later with a standalone verifier while the provider is unavailable.

semantics.crossing: One governed evaluation. The caller presents a structured request; the endpoint evaluates it against the admitted scope and issues a receipt pair: two hash-chained records, one per side, sharing one pair_id. The pair is the deliverable and the durable record of the crossing.
semantics.disposition_first: The disposition is decided before any settlement is attempted. Settlement is an eventual leg receipted onto the pair; it never alters the disposition.
semantics.fee: The fee is paid on every disposition, ALLOW or NON-ALLOW. A refusal caused by the provider's own side (a provider-side FAIL_CLOSED) never settles.
semantics.verification: Either party, or any third party, can verify a pair against the instance's public chain export without the provider's cooperation. See verification_rules.

six_field_grammar.purpose: Every NON-ALLOW disposition states exactly why, in machine-readable form — never a bare label.

4LPH4.entry_hash: SHA-256 of the canonical JSON (raw UTF-8 form) of the full entry excluding the hash field. Every entry carries prev = the previous entry's hash; the genesis entry's prev is 64 zero hex digits. Entries carry consecutive seq starting at 0.
4LPH4.export: GET /chain4.json — {verdict, problems, entries, pairs, terminal_anchor, segment}. Verify the segment yourself; do not trust the document's own verdict field.
4LPH4.pair_check: Two entries with your pair_id, kinds PAIR_A and PAIR_B, inside a segment that recomputes end to end to the document's terminal_anchor.

8374.entry_hash: sha256(prev_as_text || canonical_json(content)), hex. The genesis entry's prev is the literal string GENESIS.
8374.export: GET /chain/export.ndjson, one entry per line: {content, hash, i, prev}.
8374.pair_check: Two entries with your pair_id; index_in_pair 0 and 1; the second's pair_anchor equals the first's hash; the terminal hash equals the pair_anchor_terminal in your crossing response (or the retention bundle's anchor_after_span).

verification_rules.canonical_json: JSON with sorted keys and compact separators (',', ':') — both rails. Encoding differs by rail and is load-bearing: the 8374 rail escapes non-ASCII (ensure_ascii default, ASCII bytes); the 4LPH4 rail writes raw UTF-8 (ensure_ascii=False).
procedure: Fetch the instance's chain export (or use the span inside a retention bundle, 8374 only).
Recompute the chain from its genesis under that rail's rules: every prev link must continue the chain and every hash must recompute.
Locate your pair inside the recomputed chain and apply the rail's pair check.
A chain that recomputes end to end and contains your pair is proof the pair stands as issued. Each instance's /replay reports the provider-side verdict (MATCH) for comparison.
